answers.primary: A subagent owns this: either a one-off delegation ("use a subagent to run the integration suite and report only the failing tests with their error messages") or a saved .claude/agents/test-runner.md with tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob whose body says to return failures only. The suite executes inside the subagent's own context window and only its report comes back.
answers.rejected_alternative: A background Bash command, which runs the suite without blocking the conversation but still leaves the full log to be read into the main context rather than filtering it elsewhere.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, and the part you care about is the model's. The harness guarantees the raw output stays in the subagent's context window; what the returned summary actually contains is the subagent's judgment, not a rule.
answers.context_boundary: The suite runs in the subagent's fresh, isolated context window. Only the delegation prompt crosses in (plus CLAUDE.md and the parent git status, which non-Explore/Plan subagents load) and only the final report crosses back; your conversation history never reaches it.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when Claude delegates the test run and ends when the subagent returns its report. The raw log stops applying to your session at that moment and afterwards survives only in the subagent transcript under ~/.claude/projects/{project}/{sessionId}/subagents/agent-{agentId}.jsonl.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory. Nothing forces brevity, so a verbose subagent can paste whole failing stack dumps back and reintroduce the flood you were avoiding; conversely a terse one may drop the error text you needed. A very large log can also trigger auto-compaction inside the subagent and lose failures before the summary is written.
answers.version_caveat: No plan gate or experimental flag. As of v2.1.198 subagents run in the background by default with a narrower built-in tool set that still includes Bash, and as of v2.1.211 a background subagent's result reaches Claude as a completion notification in a later turn, so asking for results too early gets "still running".

answers.primary: A custom subagent definition in .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md with an explicit tools allowlist of Read, Grep, Glob and no Bash or PowerShell, so the harness resolves the worker's tool pool from frontmatter before it starts and Write, Edit and every shell path are simply absent.
answers.rejected_alternative: permissionMode: plan on the same subagent. It is a mode rather than a structural tool filter, and a parent session running acceptEdits or bypassPermissions takes precedence and cannot be overridden by the child.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. Tool availability is computed at launch from the definition; neither the body's instructions nor a mid-task decision by the model can add a removed tool back, and disallowedTools is applied before tools is resolved.
answers.context_boundary: Work happens in the subagent's own context window: the delegation prompt in, the review report out. The restriction needs nothing to cross the boundary, because the denied tools are never presented to that model as options.
answers.lifecycle: Applies for the life of each spawn of that subagent, from launch to final report. It lapses the moment the report returns to the main conversation, which keeps its own unrestricted tool set, so the reviewer's read-only property protects nothing after the handoff.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed. The practical cost is that dropping Bash also removes git diff, so this reviewer cannot see the change set the way the stock code-reviewer example does; hand it the diff or the file list in the prompt. If every entry in the tools list is misspelled the agent refuses to launch rather than silently running unrestricted.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.208 a tools list that resolves to no tool fails at launch with an error naming the bad entries; earlier versions launched a toolless agent that returned confusing output. Keep the file in .claude/agents/ rather than a plugin, since plugin subagents ignore permissionMode and hooks if you later want to layer those on.

answers.primary: The built-in /btw side question in interactive mode: type /btw followed by the question and the answer appears in a dismissible overlay. It is the designed inverse of a subagent, full conversation visibility with no tools.
answers.rejected_alternative: A forked subagent via /subtask, which also inherits the whole conversation but returns its result as a real message into the main transcript, which is exactly the context cost you are trying to avoid.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. The harness runs the side question outside the transcript, denies it tool access, and discards the exchange; nothing here is left to the model's discretion.
answers.context_boundary: Everything in the current conversation is visible going in; nothing comes out. The question and answer live only in the overlay and never enter conversation history, and the call reuses the parent conversation's prompt cache so the marginal cost is small.
answers.lifecycle: Fires on /btw with a question, including while Claude is mid-turn on other work, returns a single response with no follow-up turns, and stops applying when you dismiss the overlay with Space, Enter or Escape. Earlier side questions stay listed in the overlay until cleared with x.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on capability: no file reads, no commands, no search, so a question that actually needs new information gets answered from stale context and can be confidently wrong. The escape hatch is pressing f to fork the exchange into a real session with full tool access.
answers.version_caveat: Requires an interactive session; there is no /btw in headless or SDK use. /btw with no argument reopens the most recent overlay as of v2.1.212 (earlier it printed usage), Left/Right stepping through earlier answers needs v2.1.187, and forking with f is available in local sessions only.

answers.primary: A forked subagent started with /subtask, for example "/subtask draft regression tests for the bug we just characterized". A fork inherits the entire conversation so far instead of starting fresh, so every finding, ruled-out hypothesis, config quirk and stack trace is already in front of it.
answers.rejected_alternative: A named subagent such as a test-writer definition. It starts from a fresh context with only Claude's delegation message, which is precisely the re-explaining you said you do not want to do.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness owns the handoff: it copies the conversation, system prompt, tools and model into the fork and runs it in the background. The model owns whether the resulting regression tests are any good.
answers.context_boundary: The full message history crosses into the fork at spawn time. Its own tool calls stay out of your conversation and only the final result comes back, so your working context stays clean; because the system prompt and tool definitions are identical it also reuses the parent prompt cache.
answers.lifecycle: Starts when you run /subtask, runs in the background while you keep working on the fix, and ends when it posts its result into your conversation or you stop it with x in the panel. It is a snapshot: anything you and the main session discover after the fork spawned never reaches it.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open on staleness rather than blocking anything: the fork can drift from the live debugging session and draft tests against a characterization you have since revised. Its final output still lands in your main context, so a large test draft spends the context the fork was meant to protect, and a fork cannot spawn further forks.
answers.version_caveat: /subtask requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later; before that the forked-subagent command was /fork, default-on from v2.1.161. With agent view turned off, /subtask does not exist and /fork starts the forked subagent instead. CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1 or 0 forces fork mode on or off; Claude spawning forks on its own is experimental. Forks count against the 200-subagents-per-session budget.

answers.primary: A project skill at .claude/skills/pr-summary/SKILL.md carrying the written procedure, with context: fork and agent: Explore in the frontmatter so the skill content becomes the prompt for a read-only forked subagent, plus disable-model-invocation: true so the team triggers it by name with /pr-summary and Claude never starts it on its own.
answers.rejected_alternative: A custom subagent whose markdown body holds the procedure. Then the file is the system prompt and Claude writes the task prompt at delegation time, so the procedure's steps are advice to the worker rather than the literal prompt driving it.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. It creates the isolated fork context and resolves the agent type's tools, and the Explore type denies Write and Edit, so read-only is a property of the run rather than an instruction in the text.
answers.context_boundary: The rendered SKILL.md is the entire task the subagent receives. Conversation history does not cross in, and with agent: Explore neither CLAUDE.md nor git status loads. Every intermediate file read and command output stays in the fork; only the final summary returns to the invoking conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Runs on each invocation by name and ends when the fork returns its result. The isolation is scoped to that invocation only; the rest of the session is unaffected, and Explore is one-shot so there is no resuming it for a follow-up question.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on writes. The realistic failure is emptiness: a forked skill whose content reads as guidance rather than an actionable task returns nothing useful. Note also that any !`command` preprocessing in the skill runs in your session before the fork exists, so those commands are not covered by the fork's read-only tool set.
answers.version_caveat: The fork runs in the background by default and therefore gets the narrower background built-in tool set; background: false restores the full set but requires v2.1.218 or later. A user or project subagent named Explore overrides the built-in one, including its read-only guarantee. disableSkillShellExecution in managed settings turns the !`command` preprocessing off entirely.

answers.primary: The subagent's skills frontmatter field: list api-conventions under skills in the worker's definition so the full skill content, not just its description, is injected into the subagent's context at startup.
answers.rejected_alternative: Relying on CLAUDE.md or on the worker discovering the guide through the Skill tool during execution. Both are discoverable rather than guaranteed, which is the exact failure you are seeing now.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. The injection happens when the subagent launches, before the model takes its first turn, so no mid-task decision can skip it.
answers.context_boundary: The worker's starting context is its own system prompt plus environment details, Claude's delegation message, CLAUDE.md at every level of the hierarchy, git status, and the full text of each preloaded skill. The main session's conversation history and the skills it has already invoked do not cross over, which is why the main session having the guide loaded does nothing for the worker.
answers.lifecycle: Loaded at every launch of that subagent and present only for that run; nothing persists between runs. It controls what is preloaded, not what is reachable, so the worker can still invoke other skills through the Skill tool unless you remove Skill from its tools.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open, quietly. If the skill name is wrong, missing or disabled, Claude Code skips it and only logs a warning to the debug log, so the worker starts without the conventions and looks identical to today's problem. Preloading also spends the full skill's tokens on every single run.
answers.version_caveat: A skill with disable-model-invocation: true cannot be preloaded, since preloading draws from the same set Claude can invoke; as of v2.1.215 that also rules out the bundled /verify and /code-review. If you later reuse this same definition as an agent team teammate, the skills field is not applied on that path and the teammate loads skills like a normal session.

answers.primary: A subagent with tools: Bash plus a PreToolUse hook in its frontmatter matching Bash, running a validation script that reads the hook JSON from stdin, extracts tool_input.command, and exits with code 2 on any mutating statement. The system prompt telling it that it has read-only access is the soft half; the hook is the deterministic half.
answers.rejected_alternative: Bash permission deny rules in settings.json such as patterns on the database CLI invocation. Rules match command shape, not the SQL text inside the invocation, so they cannot distinguish a SELECT from an UPDATE passed to the same client.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. PreToolUse runs before the permission prompt and before execution, and exit code 2 blocks the call outright and feeds the stderr message back to the model, so an attempted mutation never reaches the database.
answers.context_boundary: The hook is a separate process outside every context window. It receives the pending tool call as JSON on stdin, and only its stderr message crosses into the subagent's context as the block reason. Nothing about the block reaches the main conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Fires before every Bash call for as long as that subagent is active and is cleaned up when it finishes. Put the same hook in settings.json instead if you want it to fire for the main session and every subagent rather than only this worker.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on what the pattern matches and open on what it does not: a keyword regex misses sp_executesql, a psql \i script.sql include, a heredoc, bcp, or a python script that opens its own connection. The worse case is operational, since a script that is not executable or that errors makes the hook fail rather than block, so test it with a deliberate UPDATE before trusting it.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.218 a project-level agent file's frontmatter hooks only run after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder, and are silently skipped (debug-log error only) until you do; user-level and --agents definitions are exempt. On Windows write the validator in PowerShell and add shell: powershell to the hook entry; on macOS and Linux chmod +x it. Plugin subagents ignore the hooks field entirely.

answers.primary: A skill the users launch by name, for example /cleanup, with disallowed-tools: AskUserQuestion in its frontmatter so that tool is removed from Claude's available pool while the skill is active. Pair it with disable-model-invocation: true so only a person can start the routine.
answers.rejected_alternative: An AskUserQuestion deny rule in permissions settings. It does block the tool, but it is session-wide and static: it does not scope to the routine and does not restore the capability by itself when the user speaks again.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. The tool is removed from the pool rather than discouraged in prose, so however stuck the routine gets there is nothing for the model to call.
answers.context_boundary: This runs in the main conversation's context, not an isolated one, unless you also add context: fork. The rendered SKILL.md enters the transcript as a single message and stays for the session; the tool restriction is turn state rather than context, so it is not part of what persists.
answers.lifecycle: Applies from the moment the skill is invoked and for the remainder of that turn, and clears automatically when the user sends their next message, which is exactly the auto-restore behavior asked for. Re-invoking the skill reapplies it.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed. The cost of that is real: a routine that genuinely needs a decision cannot ask, so it guesses or stops early with the ambiguity unresolved. Note also the asymmetry, since the skill's instructions persist in context for the rest of the session while the guardrail lapses at your next message, so the routine's guidance can outlive its restriction.
answers.version_caveat: No plan restriction or experimental flag. disallowed-tools cannot remove EndConversation while any other tool remains. Frontmatter booleans beyond true/false (yes, no, on, off, 1, 0) require v2.1.218 or later, so write true on older versions.

answers.primary: An agent team: your session becomes the lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session with its own context window, working a shared task list and messaging one another by name to try to disprove each other's theories. Ask for it explicitly and give each teammate a distinct hypothesis in the spawn prompt.
answers.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents. They get independent context too, but they report only back to the main agent and cannot message each other, so the adversarial cross-checking and shared work list you specified never happen.
answers.enforcement_owner: Model. The lead decides assignment, approves plans and synthesizes turn by turn, and teammates self-claim tasks; the harness only supplies the mailbox files, the file-locked task list, and hook events (TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted) you can exit 2 from to gate quality.
answers.context_boundary: Each teammate loads project context like a normal session (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) plus the lead's spawn prompt; the lead's conversation history does not carry over. What crosses between agents is mailbox messages and task-list state, never context, so anything a teammate must know goes in its spawn prompt or a message.
answers.lifecycle: The team forms when the first teammate spawns and lives for that session. Teammates end on a shutdown request they can approve or reject, or when the session exits; team config directories are removed then while the task list persists locally under cleanupPeriodDays.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory throughout. Claude sometimes spawns plain subagents instead of a team even when asked, teammates fail to mark tasks complete and block dependents, and the lead can declare the investigation finished early or start doing the work itself. Teammates are not isolated in worktrees, so two of them writing the same findings file overwrite each other. Token cost scales linearly with teammate count.
answers.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default: set CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment or nothing spawns. Documented behavior is as of v2.1.178, where TeamCreate and TeamDelete no longer exist and team_name on the Agent tool is ignored. Known limits: no session resumption for in-process teammates, no nested teams, permissions fixed at spawn from the lead, and split panes require tmux or iTerm2.

answers.primary: Permission deny rules in .claude/settings.json, written as Read(vendor/**) with a matching Edit(vendor/**), rather than a sentence in the rules file. The permission layer evaluates every tool call in every context, so the same rule covers delegated exploration automatically.
answers.rejected_alternative: Restating "ignore the vendor/ directory" in the delegation prompt each time research is handed off. That is the documented workaround, but it is model-owned and depends on Claude remembering to include it and the subagent honoring it.
answers.enforcement_owner: Harness. Deny is evaluated before ask and allow, a deny from any settings scope beats an allow from another, and a PreToolUse hook returning "allow" does not bypass it.
answers.context_boundary: The rule never enters a context window at all; it is checked at the tool-call boundary in the main session and inside each subagent's own window. That is precisely why it fixes this failure: the built-in Explore and Plan agents deliberately skip CLAUDE.md and the parent git status, so a rules-file sentence never reaches the agents doing the delegated searching, and there is no frontmatter field to change that.
answers.lifecycle: Loaded from settings at session start and in force for every tool call for the whole session, including subagents spawned later. It stops applying only when you edit the settings file or the session rules, and settings-file edits generally need a restart to take effect.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in Read and Edit tools, for Grep and Glob on a documented best-effort basis, and for file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash such as cat, head, tail and sed. It fails open for arbitrary subprocesses: a python or node script, or a CLI it does not recognize, can still read vendor/. Enable the sandbox if you need OS-level enforcement across all processes.
answers.version_caveat: Write the path rule on Read, not Glob: as of v2.1.210 path rules on Glob, Write, NotebookEdit or MultiEdit are accepted but never consulted and produce a startup warning. As of v2.1.208 a Read deny rule also blocks Edit on the same path, though Write and NotebookEdit still need their own Edit rule. Single-segment deny patterns like vendor/** match a vendor directory at any depth, which is the behavior you want here.
